column16: [M] Aberdeen 1942: climb from the dropped stock (in-line stock 61->81 pct hits at 50 yd). [A] climbs up and right for a right-handed shooter

[D] mp40 + suppressor mass and gas trap
[D] MP18: wooden dropped stock, side magazine. [M] MP28 burst groups moved right (Soviet 1941 trial)
[M] Soviet Dec 1941 trial: MP28 burst groups shift right (+4.8 horizontal vs +1.8 vertical over single shots)
[D] light skeleton gun, side magazine: a vertical bounce rather than a steady walk; [M] 1941 trial found it accurate
[M] Soviet Dec 1941 trial: burst groups spread mostly SIDEWAYS (+7.8 horizontal, +1.3 vertical vs single shots), 1050 rpm measured; the jacket compensator holds the muzzle down
[D] PPS-43 at a lower rate (630 measured), folding stock; drift as the PPSh, smaller
[D] 450 rpm, heavy bolt: the slowest, most controllable .45 - nearly straight up
[D] MAB 38A: heavy wooden stock and a ported compensator
[D] 8 mm Nambu is a weak round; the 1944 model's 800 rpm builds it
[D] heavy and muzzle-heavy: a big but steady, nearly vertical climb
[D] M1918 (7.25 kg, no bipod) - lighter, climbs more
[D] Lewis gun: 13 kg with the 47 rd pan - heavy, steady

[M] 2nd pattern, straight-line stock and muzzle brake; McCollum: little visible climb in SHORT bursts, long bursts walk off - the light gun's hard kick per round with a pattern that tapers early
[D] Vickers-Berthier: 11.1 kg, slow rate - very stable

[D] M1919A6 14.7 kg - held off the bipod it is a heavy, slow-rising gun
